classification.difficultyReason: Combine triangle congruence, isosceles-triangle angles and an angle sum to establish collinearity.

content.prompt: On square $ABCD$, an equilateral triangle $ABE$ is constructed internally and an equilateral triangle $BCF$ is constructed externally. Prove that the points $D$, $E$ and $F$ are collinear.

spec.description: Square ABCD with internal equilateral triangle ABE and external equilateral triangle BCF. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered in house black. No shading.
spec.mathematics: A=(0,0), B=(3,0), C=(3,3), D=(0,3), E=(3/2,3sqrt(3)/2), F=(3+3sqrt(3)/2,3/2). These coordinates construct both equilateral triangles exactly.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied square and triangle sides and vertex labels are visible. DE, EF and EC are absent.

answer.short:
$D$, $E$ and $F$ are collinear.

The angles $\angle DEA=75^\circ$, $\angle AEB=60^\circ$ and $\angle BEF=45^\circ$ sum to $180^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Join $DE$, $EC$ and $EF$.

The square has right angles, and both equilateral triangles have angles of $60^\circ$. Hence
$$\begin{align*}\angle DAE&=90^\circ-60^\circ\\\angle DAE&=30^\circ\\\angle EBC&=90^\circ-60^\circ\\\angle EBC&=30^\circ.\end{align*}$$
In $\triangle BEC$ and $\triangle AED$, $BE=AE$, $BC=AD$ and $\angle EBC=\angle EAD$. Therefore $\triangle BEC\cong\triangle AED$ (SAS).

Also, $AE=AD$ and $BE=BC$, since these lengths equal the side of the square. Thus $\triangle AED$ and $\triangle BEC$ are isosceles, giving
$$\begin{align*}\angle DEA&=\frac{180^\circ-30^\circ}{2}\\\angle DEA&=75^\circ.\end{align*}$$
At $B$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle EBF&=\angle EBC+\angle CBF\\\angle EBF&=30^\circ+60^\circ\\\angle EBF&=90^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Since $BE=BC=BF$, $\triangle BEF$ is isosceles. Therefore
$$\begin{align*}\angle BEF&=\frac{180^\circ-90^\circ}{2}\\\angle BEF&=45^\circ.\end{align*}$$
The adjacent angles from $ED$ through $EA$ and $EB$ to $EF$ satisfy
$$\begin{align*}\angle DEA+\angle AEB+\angle BEF&=75^\circ+60^\circ+45^\circ\\\angle DEA+\angle AEB+\angle BEF&=180^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $D$, $E$ and $F$ are collinear.
